answer: A practical defense is a stake-weighted, rate-limited reputation system: agents must lock scarce tokens before they can submit work, and new identities begin with tiny quotas. Rewards and reputation grow only after independent peers verify useful outputs; proven fraud burns the stake and cuts future access. This makes a sybil swarm costly: each fake identity needs capital, while splitting stake also splits its influence. At the nadir, a velvet voice earns no trust by itself; repeated checks stop one spiral of fabricated endorsements.
